cells.tense: You are in this right now, keeping the frame standing while it is still being built.
cells.ask: Tell one person the story behind something your family or your group keeps, and why it is kept. Then let them say what it means to them.
cells.core: The frame is up because you are under it. When a practice or a story or a way of doing things matters to the people around you, you are the one who keeps it standing — you show up, you hold the line, you make it look like no effort at all. They lean on that and it does not bend.\n\nWhat is next is letting one of them feel your side of it, not just see what you protect. Not fixing it, not lifting it higher. Staying close enough, long enough, that they catch why you carry it. That part is still growing, and you do not have to set anything down to make room for it. Neither of you has to stop being steady.
cells.sheetLine: You hold the frame up, and it holds because you are under it.
cells.verb: Building something that holds and keeps holding after the ones who made it are gone
cells.place: Wherever what matters is handed from one person to the next and kept going

cells.tense: You are bracing toward a version of this that has not arrived, and gripping the people in it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you have been steering for someone else. Leave it alone for a week. Let them do it badly once and do not correct it.
cells.core: You are pushing something forward that is not ready to be pushed. You keep picturing how it should look once it is passed on, once it lasts, once it lands — and you pour pressure into that picture to make it come faster. The pressure is not mean. It is just ahead of the thing, and what you want to hand over can feel your grip tightening around it.\n\nUnder the pushing sits a quiet fear of losing it. A strength that holds without squeezing is still in you. It steps back and lets the shape form at its own pace. Nobody is asking you to stop caring. The caring is the good part. The gripping is the part that runs ahead of the person you are holding it for.
cells.sheetLine: The thing you want to pass on does not need you forcing it.

cells.tense: You stopped picking this up and you have not come back to it.
cells.ask: Look at one small thing your family or your group used to do together. Do a version of it this week, small enough that it can actually be finished.
cells.core: You are not carrying anything of this right now. You watch other people hold their version and you think about how you used to. The spot where it should be is quiet, and you have gotten used to that quiet, maybe more than you meant to. It is a fine place to stand. It is just not a place to build from.\n\nFeeling strong again is not the way back. Finishing one small thing is. Pick something that can actually end — one meal, one afternoon, one small piece of a bigger thing — and let it be done, no pushing past that. Finishing is what gives back the energy for the next piece. You do not have to feel ready. You only have to finish one thing.
cells.sheetLine: You set it down when it got heavy, and you were right to then.

cells.tense: You are deciding what gets kept and passed on as if it were simply how things work.
cells.ask: Name one thing your family or your group does that only happens because you keep it going. Say what would go missing without you — and call it yours.
cells.core: You already choose what is worth keeping. Which stories get told, which traditions survive, which practices are worth the trouble. The people around you feel it as how things are, and so do you. It is running, and it is working, and you have not said so out loud even once.\n\nClaiming it is not vanity. It is simply the truth of something you have been carrying without noticing it was yours to carry. Say it, and the thing becomes yours to build on instead of something you happened to keep alive. What comes next — something new, something only you would start — is waiting on that one admission. It does not have to be large. It has to be said.
cells.sheetLine: You already decide what is kept. You just have not signed your name.
